claims.statement: Laplace 1774 memoir distinguished effects with known cause and inferred unknown causes from observed effects
Stigler English translation is a later scholarly edition, not 1774 first French printing
Laplace's studies linked finite differences, probability and methods of analysis
BnF catalogs Paris first edition of Théorie analytique des probabilités in 1812
1814 Essai philosophique was a later broader explanatory work separate from 1812 first edition
Historical research links Laplace probability research to astronomical observations, errors, and celestial mechanics
Modern independent measurement likelihood is product of error density values given model
Bayesian normalization divides prior times likelihood by an integral of total mass
Gaussian type concentration integral ∫exp(-nt²/2) about a sharp peak scales as sqrt(2pi/n)
Fixed systematic measurement bias is not removed by averaging independent zero-mean fluctuations
Modern asymptotic Laplace approximation does not assume all posteriors are smooth single-peaked
